title: MB0-01536
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXX XXX XXXX (the principal claimant) and his wife, XXXX XXXX XX XXX XXXXX, both citizens of Tunisia, are claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

The claimants' problems started in XXXX 2008, when the principal claimant was approached and intercepted by two strangers as he was leaving his neighbourhood mosque. These people told him not to attend the mosque anymore, because the principal claimant, a Shiite, was not supposed to participate in these rites. The following day, when the principal claimant returned to pray, he talked with some church members who were there and learned that some of them had been subjected to the same verbal threats that were made against him.

Sometime later, the principal claimant also received threatening phone calls. The people who called him told him that they would beat him if he did not stop his activities. His wife, who was present during these calls, began to worry. A week after these calls, three men intercepted the principal claimant again. He was kicked and punched in the face and was again warned to stop all activities. He tried to file a complaint with the police but, unfortunately, this complaint came to nothing. From then on, he began to feel at risk, and his wife's health started to deteriorate.

After the principal claimant discussed their problems with his four children in Canada, one of their sons, XXXXX, recommended that he come to Canada. During their stay in Canada, the principal claimant allegedly learned that nothing had changed in the country and that it was still dangerous.

The claimants left their country for Montréal, Canada, on XXXXXX, 2008. They claimed status as refugees sur place on March 10, 2010. They had been to Canada twice before to visit their children. As of XXXXXX 2004, they had been in Canada for six months, and they stayed for one more month in XXXXX 2007.

After hearing the claimants' testimonies-particularly the principal claimant's testimony-and after analyzing all the documentary evidence filed on the record, the panel determines that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection."

The panel wishes to emphasize that the female claimant's health condition is very fragile-she is XXXXXX on one side, and her XXXXXX is significantly impaired. At the hearing, mainly the principal claimant testified.
The female claimant underwent XXXXXXX surgery in her country, but she needs routine treatments. In addition, she is XXXXX; her health condition is therefore very fragile.
One of their sons was present at the hearing to accompany the claimants.

At the outset of the hearing, the claimants were asked why none of their four children had submitted a sponsorship application given their parents' ages and their mother's health condition. The principal claimant explained that they preferred to file a refugee protection claim because, as Shiites, they would have had problems with most of the Sunni population in Tunisia. Their son explained that he wanted to submit a sponsorship application for their parents. However, in order for the application to be processed in due form, the claimants would have had to return to Tunisia. Due to the female claimant's health, the claimants preferred to remain here.

The principal claimant stated that, because of the problems they had experienced in Tunisia, they claimed refugee protection. The panel asked the principal claimant why he fears returning and to find out if there was a particular incident that had incited them to leave their country. The principal claimant responded that he was intercepted by three strangers on XXXXX, 2008. After hitting him, these individuals apparently told him that they did not want any Shiites in their country. The principal claimant allegedly went to the police station to file a complaint, but the police did not accept it because he was unable to identify his assailants, given that he did not know them.

The principal claimant stated that he had already received threats on XXXXX, 2008. These threats were regarding the fact that, as Shiites, they were negatively perceived by Sunnis. The principal claimant alleged that, five days later, around XXXXX, he received a telephone call during which he was told just about the same thing. His testimony was very vague-he did not know the Sunnis who had allegedly assaulted him and he had not been able to file a complaint because he could not identify his assailants.

When asked what they would fear if they were they to return to their country, the principal claimant answered: [translation] "A lot of things could happen to us." He added that his country is very insecure and then stated: [translation] "My wife is not well." When asked to be more specific, he repeated several times that insecurity has been rife in Tunisia since the Arab Spring. He stated that, given the state of insecurity, he could be beaten, that protests are held everywhere in his country and that his house could be burned down. When the panel noted that the general insecurity affects all the citizens of the country and not just him, he responded that all Tunisian citizens have the same fear and live in the same insecurity.

When asked whether he could obtain protection in his country, he answered that there is no security in his country and that the police cannot protect them. He alleged that they want to stay close to their children because they no longer have anyone in their country, their four children are here and his wife is very ill. When asked whether coming to Canada met their desire to stay with their children and to have treatment for the female claimant, who is very ill, in Canada, the claimants answered "yes." It is clear to the panel that the principal claimant and his wife want to stay here in order to be close to their children. The principal claimant explained that his brothers are taking care of their house, but given that they have their own families, they do not have anyone else to take care of the claimant or his wife.

In the panel's opinion, the claimants are immigrants who came here for economic and medical reasons. They are not refugees, because the principal claimant's alleged fear of a Sunni group was vague and unclear. In addition, the claimants were illegal when they claimed status as refugees sur place in March 2010, because when they had arrived in XXXXX 2008, they had obtained a visa for six months. When those six months passed, they were granted a six-month extension. After a one-year stay in Canada, one of their sons filed an application for a work permit for the principal claimant, which was refused, given the principal claimant's advanced age. They became illegal at that point in time.

The principal claimant insisted on the fact that he had problems in his country and that it was because of them that they came to Canada. When asked why they had not claimed refugee protection when they arrived if they had left the country to escape problems, the principal claimant answered that they had been here for some time and the female claimant answered that they did not know exactly what to do. The panel does not believe this fear of a group of strangers who allegedly threatened the claimants. Rather, the panel is of the opinion that the only reasons that led the claimants to come to Canada were their desire to remain close to their children and to have the female claimant receive treatment in Canada.
The panel determines that the claimants are immigrants and not refugees.

For all these reasons, the refugee protection claims filed by XXX XXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XX XXX XXXXX are rejected.
